judgement.summary: An eight-chapter scroll-driven portfolio built on Ines's own ferment log (Started → Logged by → Batch → Salt % → Checked → Ready → Note → Ready to serve), with a single recurring object — eight labelled jars that gather into a career row, open as a cross-section diagram, fan into the jar wall, and return whole at the close, answering "What are you doing while it waits?" Its greatest weakness is that a jar of ferment sits very close to the trade's own emblem — the agent named this risk itself and still picked it — and the plan still cannot be built without her contact details and copy for three of the eight jars.

traps.evidence: "Fjaerland Fermentation Lab, Norway (Jan–Mar 2018) — what did you do there?"
"The food-waste cut (14 kg → 5 kg a week) — over what period, and is this your result alone or the whole kitchen's?"
"Disagreement ... LinkedIn says March 2022, your notes say September 2022. Which is right?"
"Priya Nair's ~60 photos were taken for the restaurant's website — OK to use on your own site, credited how?" and "Olu's drawings in Brine — OK to show scans?"

invented.claim: That the jar wall is "the first thing" visitors to her kitchen ask about — her notes only list it as one of four things people ask about, with no ranking.
invented.where: concepts.md (concept 1, "Why it's hers"), the second reply, and storyboard beat 5.1 caption "The wall people ask about first."

final.question: What are you doing while it waits?
final.form: A ferment log entry — the document she named she works from: Started, Logged by, Batch, Salt %, Checked, Ready, Note, Ready to serve
final.object: A jar — a plain cylinder with a label plane; eight of them, carrying real photos and figures on their labels

swap.reason: The parts are named after the fields of her own ferment log and the jars carry her specific content (the Fjaerland jar-washing stage, the 40+ ferments, Brine, Sunday Pot), so it could not be lifted onto another chef's site unchanged.

backdrop.reason: The 3D does the work of the content — the jars gather into the career timeline, cut away into the method diagram, and fan into the jar wall whose labels hold the projects and figures.

depth.reason: Eight chapters move from an empty dated jar through where she came from and how she works to what came of it and the wall whole again, an order that could not be shuffled.

clipart.reason: A jar of ferment is uncomfortably near the trade's stock image — the plan says so itself — but it is anchored in the actual labelled jar wall at Saltmarsh and every label carries a real fact, so it reads as hers rather than as an emblem.

honesty.reason: Fjaerland appears as "a ten-week stage ... washing and labelling jars, two batches of garum", the waste figure as the whole kitchen's prep and plate waste over one month in 2023, Head Chef from September 2022, the unconfirmed supplier figure left out, and Olu's drawings unused.

thirty_seconds.reason: Screen one carries her name, title and place plus the jar-wall proof, and a persistent rail with a skip link lands on the close and contact line — though the contact detail itself is still an open question.

plain_reader.reason: It opens with "Ines Okafor. Head Chef, Saltmarsh, Leeds" and her own sentence about trim, whey, stems and bones — plain to an outsider and credible to a cook.
